summary: Scoped review prototype for automatic formative completion XP: verified enrollment, live selected-class reads, private reflections, exact catalog validation, derived totals, immutable ranking owner/alias and no grade publication. Existing staff-wide academic trust is not a complete tenant ACL. Not deployed.

findings.issue: Owners can forge completion of known mission IDs through a modified client, even though arbitrary totals, duplicates and unknown IDs are denied. XP therefore records formative claims, not verified mastery.
findings.recommendation: Keep school grades and high-stakes rewards separate. Review a server-authoritative, idempotent attempt validator before treating game or mission scores as certified results. No Functions deployment is included.

findings.issue: Existing academic instructor access remains broader than per-class authorization across all legacy modules. Analytics assignments alone do not establish tenant isolation.
findings.recommendation: Complete a separately reviewed tenant/section ACL migration before admitting unrelated institutions or untrusted instructors.

findings.issue: Class documents contain opaque roster/owner IDs in addition to UI aliases. Transferred or deleted roster profiles can leave stale alias rows until resynchronization or controlled cleanup.
findings.recommendation: Disclose that aliases are pseudonyms, not anonymity. Design an audited membership-lifecycle projection if stronger unlinkability or immediate row removal is required; do not enable unattended cleanup implicitly.

findings.issue: Client ranking synchronization reads four course records. Class lists are capped at 500 and cannot claim a global position when truncated.
findings.recommendation: Retain emulator budget coverage and the partial-list label. Reassess aggregate cost, paging and authoritative rank projections if classes or course catalogs expand.
